chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How ugly is poverty after wealth, and how ugly is sinning after destitution, and how ugly is sinning after wealth, and how ugly is sinning after destitution, and uglier than that is the one who worships Allah then leaves his worship.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say is uglier than poverty or sin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual peril of inconsistency, particularly highlighting that abandoning established worship is more grievous than the transient states of poverty or sin. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the value of steadfastness (istiqamah) in devotion, suggesting that the loss of a practiced spiritual habit carries a heavier weight than temporary worldly or moral struggles. The narration serves as a warning against spiritual regression after having attained a state of piety.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘How ugly is the poverty after the enrichment, and the ugliness of the sinning after the destitution, and uglier than that is the worship of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then leaving His<sup>azwj</sup> worship’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘How ugly is poverty after riches, sin in destitution and worst of all worshipping Allah and then giving up His worship.’”
